limitations: The evidence items are context because their timing or measures do not fully match the contract.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is not good, reliable software: it is inherently inconsistent and unreliable, inefficient, financially ruinous, and increases users' cognitive load.

statement.excerpt: A.I. is not even good, reliable software! It resembles the death of the art of technology — inconsistent and unreliable by definition, inefficient by design, financially ruinous, and ADDS to the cognitive load of the user by requiring them to be ever-vigilant.
statement.document_title: How To Argue With An AI Booster

our_interpretation: Treat 'death of the art of technology' and 'good' as evaluative rhetoric; assess the factual assertions about reliability, efficiency, financial harm and user workload.
Read added cognitive load as a net increase relative to doing comparable work without generative AI, including checking and correction.
Read inefficiency as resources required per acceptable completed task, not merely the presence of computing costs.
For this ongoing observation with no stated period, use the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, April–June 2025. Earlier or insufficiently dated measurements are context only.
The claim does not identify whose finances are ruined, a monetary measure, or an accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations show unreliable task completion, inefficient resource use and increased total user workload, while comparable financial records establish the asserted financial harm for a defined population.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show dependable useful performance, efficient task completion or reduced total workload sufficient to refute the corresponding generalizations; financial contradiction requires a defined company population and matching accounting measure.

evidence.locator: Abstract; manuscript sections IV-B and IV-C
evidence.explanation: The study provides material counterevidence to an inevitable increase in workload, using task comparisons and workload questionnaires in a small sample. The retrieved passages do not establish exact experiment dates within April–June, so it remains context rather than decisive period-matched evidence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Period-matched evaluations covering reliability, resources and total workload across a defined set of products and users, plus an identified financial entity, measure and accounting basis.
